clue.text: Out of many directions, soldiers returned in formal line beside lodgings

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters already sitting inside the word formal are turned round where they stand

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for soldiers
quarters are rooms where people are lodged

explanation.surface: A report of troops coming back and standing in a neat row next to their billets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formal' looks like a description of the line, but the soldiers are already inside it: they turn round where they stand rather than being added.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning from every side or source, i.e. from many directions at once.

clue.text: Type of lorry winged beast escaped, so Spooner says

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the two words here trade their beginnings

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal
fled means ran away, escaped

explanation.surface: A bat got loose, and someone wants to know what kind of truck that was.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of BAT and FLED gives FLAT and BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatbed is a lorry or truck with an open, flat platform for carrying loads and no sides.

clue.text: Not running, aluminium internal parts

parts.note: a machine that is off is not running
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: An engine at rest with its aluminium components on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs of a slaughtered animal, its edible inner parts.

clue.text: Stirrers from Costa no cost — gratis to put another way

indicators.note: saying something another way rearranges it, so these letters are reordered
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the word cost taken out of Costa leaves just its final letter

explanation.surface: Coffee stirrers handed out free at a Costa café, phrased differently.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa without cost leaves A; add GRATIS and TO and rearrange. Costa is a British coffee-shop chain, which makes 'stirrers' look like coffee sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitators are troublemakers who stir up unrest, people who stir things up.

clue.text: Machine that turns coffee making low temperature hot

indicators.note: the coffee is made over by letting one letter become another

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
T for temperature, the lower of the two in the word as written down the grid
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A coffee machine that heats a cool drink into a hot one.
explanation.walkthrough: In LATTE the second, lower T (temperature) becomes H (hot); in a down entry the later letter sits lower.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a workshop machine that spins a piece of wood or metal so it can be shaped.

clue.text: Funds removed from banks I had cancelled

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outer letters, and these are taken away

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone withdrew their money from the banks and called off their plans.
explanation.walkthrough: Funds without its banks (first and last letters) is UND.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo an action is to reverse or annul it, so undid is a synonym of cancelled.

clue.text: Partygoer comparatively bold removing top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: braver is the comparative of brave, bold

explanation.surface: A clubber who is bolder than the rest, so much so they lose their shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who goes to raves, lively all-night dance parties.

clue.text: Digging Eastern illustrations around hotel

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the hotel letter, enclosing it

parts.note: artwork is the illustrations in a book or magazine
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pictures from the East hung around a hotel being excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthwork is excavation and embankment construction, so it covers the job of digging out ground.

clue.text: Writers Laurence and Laurie discussed in rigorous way

indicators.note: discussing something is talking about it out loud, so the names are heard rather than read

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy and Laurie Lee wrote Cider with Rosie; their two surnames run together are what is heard

explanation.surface: Two English authors talked about with strict seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: STERNE plus LEE, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sternly means doing it severely and strictly, which is acting in a rigorous manner.

clue.text: Distress when a French copper cuts foot

indicators.note: the policeman cuts into the foot's letters, sitting between them

parts.note: flic is French slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A Paris policeman injures someone's foot, causing pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To afflict is to trouble or cause suffering, so it is a verb synonym of distress.

clue.text: Various waterfowl close to lake

parts.note: divers are diving water birds, called loons in North America

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is used

explanation.surface: Several kinds of water bird gathered near a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means of many kinds, a close synonym of various.

clue.text: Wood like dog's brought back

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'
dog is is a Lab, short for Labrador; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A dog retrieving a stick of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood from a tropical tree, used for models.

clue.text: Swimming in her pond is a mood booster

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about freely and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A dip in her pond lifts her spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorphins are hormones released in the brain, for example during exercise, that lift one's spirits.

clue.text: Casino built outside Italy's capital city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside the capital, around it
something built is constructed from parts, so these letters are assembled anew
a capital letter here is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gambling house constructed on the edge of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus, a city on that Mediterranean island.

clue.text: Cook rhubarb with fish? That's revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: rhubarb and rot are both slang for nonsense
cod is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: A chef proposing a radical dish of rhubarb with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to tamper with or falsify it, the same as to cook the books.

clue.text: Merry prisoner court dismissed on the bottle

indicators.note: in a down clue one part placed on another sits above it
dismissing the court sends its letters away from the prisoner's word

parts.note: a convict is a prisoner
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A cheerful inmate, let off by the judge, takes to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Convivial means friendly and lively, especially at a party, so it is a synonym of merry.

clue.text: Padded copper ring with gleaming exterior

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the gleaming word forms the exterior, wrapped around the ring

parts.note: shiny means gleaming
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A soft copper ring with a polished surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushiony describes something soft and well-stuffed, like a cushion, so it means padded.

clue.text: Advantage in competition from loaf, singular baked item

parts.note: loaf is slang for the head, as in 'use your loaf'
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tart is a baked pastry

explanation.surface: A baker gets ahead in a contest with one loaf and one pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an early lead given to a contestant, an edge over rivals in a race.

clue.text: Urges to grasp core of definitive disciplines

indicators.note: the first word holds the other in its grip, enclosing it

parts.note: pushes means urges, presses

indicators.note: the core is the centre, the middle two letters of the ten

explanation.surface: Someone presses to get to the heart of a final ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline someone is to penalise them, so disciplines here is a verb meaning punishes.

clue.text: Albatross regularly following sound from cork trees

indicators.note: the picked letters follow the sound, coming after it

parts.note: a pop is the sound a cork makes leaving a bottle

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A seabird follows the popping of a champagne cork into the cork trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplars are tall, fast-growing trees of the willow family.

clue.text: Ball that's targeted article by large canine

parts.note: in the British lawn game of bowls the jack is the small ball players aim at
a is the indefinite article
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A dog chases a ball that has been aimed at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackal is a wild member of the dog family, so it is an example of a canine.

clue.text: Roast meat put with reduced wine

parts.note: lamb is meat from a young sheep

indicators.note: a reduced word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A recipe: meat roasted with a wine reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them harshly, the same as to lambast them.

clue.text: Stickybeaks in conversation care about lottery

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken aloud, so this word is heard rather than read

parts.note: stickybeak is Australian slang for a nosy person, and as a verb it means pries

indicators.note: about means turned round here, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a ward is a person in someone's care, and ward also means guardianship

explanation.surface: Nosy parkers gossiping about who cares who wins the lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize draw is a raffle in which winners are drawn at random, a kind of lottery.

clue.text: Consumed all contents from set rate menu

indicators.note: the contents of each word are its letters inside the first and last, taken from all three

explanation.surface: Every dish on a fixed-price menu has been finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten means swallowed as food, a synonym of consumed in the sense of eating.

clue.text: Further test son's taken in two subjects

indicators.note: the son is taken into the subjects, placed between them

parts.note: RE (religious education) and IT (information technology) are two school subjects
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son retaking exams in two school subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an exam taken again after failing, a second attempt at the same test.

clue.text: Superfluous part of garment, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the waist is the part of a dress or trousers around the middle

explanation.surface: Someone is informed that a bit of their clothing is unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste as an adjective means surplus or no longer needed, as in waste material.

clue.text: Multitude of cycling heats

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: warms means heats

explanation.surface: A crowd of riders in qualifying cycle races.
explanation.walkthrough: Heats look like rounds of a cycle race but they are the verb heats (warms).
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large, dense crowd, a synonym of multitude.

clue.text: A bathroom fixture lacking base and stand

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, the last letter, which is missing

parts.note: a bidet is a low basin found in some bathrooms

explanation.surface: A bathroom fitting without a base, plus a stand to hold it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide can mean to tolerate, as in 'I can't stand him', a verb synonym of stand.

clue.text: Posh folk taken from Paris to Sicily

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Rich travellers being flown from Paris down to Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristos is informal for aristocrats, the upper-class nobility.

clue.text: Parts of plants sustained energy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old plural of stamen, the pollen-bearing organ of a flower

explanation.walkthrough: The botanical sense is rare: stamina is an old plural of stamen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both flower organs that produce pollen and the endurance needed to keep going.

clue.text: Roughly nine letters Matt is sending to Coventry

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Matt writes about nine letters to someone in Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them; Coventry is an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The silent treatment is deliberately ignoring someone, which is just what that idiom means.
